entries.description: A Sigma list (dropdown) filter control with no selection shows the text "All" in light grey placeholder styling. Tableau's quick filter shows "(All)" or "All" in normal dark text. The control also has Sigma's own chevron and border chrome instead of Tableau's quick-filter look. The word "All" is correct, but its lighter, muted text color and weight differ from the source.
entries.evidence: Schema: the public OpenAPI `components.schemas.Control.oneOf` list variant declares `placeholder` (string, "Placeholder text shown while the control has no value"), so the prior claim that it exists only on text/number/date is refuted. It also has `allOption` (shown|hidden), which only affects the picker row. Probe A (workbook 330560dd-b83d-432a-841b-dba64c2c0bdf, A.png, which I viewed): with `placeholder: "All"` on multiple, single, and allOption-hidden controls, the closed control renders "All" and the default renders "Select values". The table stays unfiltered with 4 rows. Probe B (55729abc-7f06-4843-b300-f516b9cc370c) and the skeptic2 probe (f21eb1f1-05c1-4b15-8def-babdec84b05c): `color` and `fontWeight` added alongside the placeholder return POST 200 but are dropped on GET-back, and the render is still grey. Selecting all values renders "(4) East, West, North, South". `values: ["All"]` renders a black chip, and the table shows "No data". Verdict record: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-sigma-platform-difference-verdicts.json (live probe, 2026-11-05).

entries.description: A Sigma region, point or geography map shows Mapbox basemap place labels (city and state names) on the map canvas, and no API or SDK setting hides them. Near the element edges they can be clipped or crowd the filled regions, while the Tableau source map has no basemap labels, or different ones. Only the basemap's own text labels differ.
entries.evidence: Schema: in the OpenAPI, CommonElement oneOf[14], [15] and [16] (point-map, region-map and geography-map) define mapStyle as oneOf {baseStyle light|dark|streets|satellite, allowZoom, accessToken} | {baseStyle:'custom', styleUrl} | {styleUrl} | null. It has no label, place or POI visibility property. A grep of openapi.json finds showLabels only on the pivot table. The SDK regionMap, pointMap and geographyMap methods have no basemap or label setter. Live probes: mapStyle {baseStyle:'light', hideLabels:true} returned 200 and the key was dropped on GET-back (workbook fddf30a9-a73b-44ca-85df-a9171bddc4b4). showLabels, labels, placeLabels and showPlaceLabels returned 200 and were all dropped (67f68bd3-6f04-4328-abc8-8e5b98a627bd). Removing labels works only through a custom styleUrl: empty-v9 (20639795) removes the land too, and satellite-v9 (b4c050ed) is imagery only. Verdict record: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-sigma-platform-difference-verdicts.json (live probe, 2026-11-05).

entries.description: Horizontal bar chart: Tableau shows a small, upright header over the category (row) axis. The Sigma chart either has no category-axis title at all (the default when the title is omitted) or, when a title is set, shows it as text rotated 90 degrees running vertically along the left of the category axis. The look matches only when the header is hidden, or when it is moved to a separate text element or the chart title above the chart frame.
entries.evidence:
**Schema:** In the OpenAPI bar-chart spec, `xAxis.format.title` accepts only `text`, `fontSize`, `color` and `fontWeight`. `xAxis.format` has no title orientation, angle or position field. The only angle field is `labels.labelAngle`, which applies to tick labels. The only `titleOrient` field is the KPI one (top or bottom). The SDK axis offers `set_title`, `set_show_title`, `set_title_font_size`, `set_title_color`, `set_title_bold` and `set_label_angle`, with no title rotation.

**Live probes (three independent agents, all on <redacted>.ORDER_FACT):**
- Setting `title.text` renders the title rotated 90 degrees vertically (workbook 2c8635f1).
- Adding orientation, angle, rotation, textOrientation, titleOrient, position or titleAngle at the title level or the format level still returns 200. The GET-back drops every one of those keys, and the render is unchanged (workbooks 2c8635f1 and 54a117a9).
- Setting `labels.labelAngle=0` leaves the title vertical (workbook d9f3a8d6).
- Empty title text is rejected with a 400.
- `visibility: "hidden"` hides the tick labels as well (workbook 4092061a).
- Omitting the title renders no category-axis title (workbook 47758456). Verdict record: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-sigma-platform-difference-verdicts.json (live probe, 2026-11-05).

entries.description: When a number does not fit its space, Tableau shows '###' and Sigma shows the value cut off with an ellipsis (e.g. '$266...', '$197,67...', or '$...' in table cells, pivot cells, and KPI tiles). The overflow marker differs: Sigma has no '###' mode, so a grader will never see '###' in Sigma.
entries.evidence:
Schema (openapi.json):
- No property for '###', ellipsis, shrinkToFit or truncate on cell or KPI text.
- `truncation` is date-bucket truncation only.
- `CommonElement.overflow` (clip or scroll) applies to containers only.
- `Table.columns[].style.width` is in px and overrides auto-sizing.
- `textWrap` takes wrap or clip.
- `TableStyle.autofitColumns` takes shown or hidden.
- Pivot `display.bodyWidths.uniformWidth` is available.
- `kpi-chart.value.fontSize` is available.

Live probes, all HTTP 200 with fields persisted on GET-back:
- Workbook 0abc29a1 (a.png): `width:45` rendered '$266...' and 'Net Re...'. Adding `textWrap` or `autofitColumns` still truncated. No width rendered the full '$266.37'.
- Workbook 184f4f54: `width:100` and the default both rendered full values. `autofitColumns` alone had no effect.
- Workbook f43c0898: a narrow KPI rendered '$197,676,5...'. `width:40` with `wrap` split the first row into '$266 / .37' and showed '$17...' on the other rows.
- Workbooks 1dd3b60f and 56d87596 (k.png, k2.png), KPI tile about 100px wide: fontSize 14 rendered '$197,67...' and fontSize 10 rendered the full '$197,676.50'.

No probe produced '###'. Verdict record: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-sigma-platform-difference-verdicts.json (live probe, 2026-11-05).

entries.description: Native Sigma navigation buttons can match a Tableau text-button tab strip in fill color, text color, bold, square corners and equal full-cell width, but some details differ. (a) A filled tab cannot also carry a distinct colored border. The border-only outline variant is always a thin 1px line. (b) Label font size snaps to three steps (small/medium/large). The font family is the Sigma theme font, not Tableau's font. (c) There are no hover effects and no real active-tab state. The highlighted tab is static per page. (d) Inner padding and button height are fixed, so a tall Tableau tab renders as a shorter button centered in its cell. A grader sees tabs with the right colors and widths but slightly different label size, font and border thickness.
entries.evidence:
Schema: the public OpenAPI CommonElement button (kind "button") has properties name, appearance, align, size, borderRadius, fillColor, fontColor, fontWeight, icon, actions and popover only. It has no borderColor, borderWidth, fontSize, fontFamily, width, height, padding or style.

Probe good (12895ecd): fill, fontColor, bold, size large, square corners and stretch persisted and rendered. good.png showed a navy full-cell tab and a light tab.

Probe bad (72573ea1): borderColor, fontSize, width and style were accepted with 200, but all four were dropped on GET-back and had no visual effect.

Probe sk2 (66da1818): an outline button with fillColor #FF0000 or #999999 persisted the value and rendered a thin custom-colored border (sk2.png). The SDK calls set_border, set_background_color and set_padding on the button were rejected with "styling is not supported on this element (type 'button')". set_page_tabs_hidden_in_view_mode persisted.

Probe sk1 (40732913): an image element with actions plus style.borderWidth 3 and borderColor persisted and rendered (img.png). This is a workaround only, with an SVG-baked label. Verdict record: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-sigma-platform-difference-verdicts.json (live probe, 2026-11-05).

entries.description: Sigma text renders in Lato (or Arial), a similar humanist sans, rather than Tableau's proprietary Tableau Book. A grader comparing side by side may still see small glyph differences, such as letter widths, numeral shapes and x-height, in titles, KPI numbers, axis labels and table text. The overall look is the same sans family. The typeface is the same across the whole workbook, so a Tableau dashboard that mixes fonts on individual titles cannot be matched element by element.
entries.evidence:
Schema: settings.theme.overrides.fonts has textFont and dataFont, both free-form strings (dataFont defaults to Roboto) in the public OpenAPI. No per-title font family exists: name takes only text/fontSize/color, and titleFont takes only color/fontSize/fontWeight. Live probes in folder b9629e9d:
- Lato for both fonts (52b73b84-51be-4abf-b468-962637f48c92 and 5f03b516-f0b6-4351-947d-84fc1da102f4), Arial (afbf1907-43f2-43ed-9f5b-15c176a8903d) and Georgia (41e83b31-94f9-45ff-bef5-6ff3a334055a) all persisted on GET-back. The renders changed the KPI title and value, chart titles, axis labels, table headers and table cells.
- Merriweather textFont (bfb21406-772a-44f4-894e-d1d930d2d940) rendered serif titles.
- Roboto Mono dataFont (f08a48ae-8b91-4733-9146-c7184f73b2c6) rendered monospace data.
- Playfair Display, Lora and Courier New persisted but fell back silently to the default.
- Tableau Book is not in Sigma's font set, so an exact match is not possible. Verdict record: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-sigma-platform-difference-verdicts.json (live probe, 2026-11-05).

entries.description: Residual, not a gap. On STACKED bar charts the dataLabel.anchor setting has no visible effect. A grader sees each segment's value label centered inside the segment, white by default, even when anchor is "outside-end". The labels never move above the stack. Only the text color can be changed, through dataLabel.color. Single-series and clustered bars place dark labels just past the bar end, which matches Tableau. Exact label font and gap from the bar differ slightly from Tableau. Stacked-total labels above the stack (Tableau's 'show totals') were not probed; the dataLabel.totals property exists in the schema but is unverified.
entries.evidence:
Schema: probes/openapi.json CommonElement/oneOf[0]/oneOf[2]/allOf[1]/properties/dataLabel.anchor enum is auto|end|middle|outside-end|start. Live probes in folder b9629e9d:
- 6b8d82f3 (outside-end) and f81c3dba (horizontal, color #222222, bold) render dark labels outside the bar end, and the readback kept the fields.
- d59cd885 (end) renders white labels inside the bar. I viewed the PNG.
- eee9b894 (clustered, stacking none) renders labels outside.
- Stacked 3ea127f2 and 964fb000 with outside-end render identically to the no-anchor stacked baseline 6bf6b75e, with white labels centered in each segment. I viewed stack_oe.png. The anchor persisted on GET but had no effect.
- 4ea7c66e (stacked, color #222222) renders dark labels inside the segments.
- anchor "bogus-pos" was rejected with a masked 400. Verdict record: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-sigma-platform-difference-verdicts.json (live probe, 2026-11-05).

entries.description: On a pivot table, a null dimension member's row or column header can only be blank (the default). A custom label such as "(none)" or "Unknown" does not apply: column format.displayNullAs on a pivot dimension persists but has no effect, and getting the label means rewriting the data with a Coalesce formula.
entries.evidence:
Schema: displayNullAs exists only on format kind "number", under Table.columns[].format, Table.metrics[].format and conditionalFormats[].style.format. The kind "datetime" format strips it on GET (sk2 date, wb ee70f32a). kind "text" is rejected with POST 400.

Probes in org <redacted>:
- wb c8646607 (sk1): pivot null row headers rendered blank by default, and the pivot measure rendered "N/A".
- wb 1148a374 and wb 56678614 (sk2): pivot null row and column headers rendered blank. displayNullAs on the pivot dimension had no effect.

The PNGs were checked directly: sk1.png. Verdict record: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-sigma-platform-difference-verdicts.json (live probe, 2026-11-05).

entries.description: A Sigma pivot table's data rows have a fixed height set by the table's cellSpacing preset (extra-small, small, medium or large); they do not stretch to fill a taller tile the way Tableau's entire-view crosstab rows do. When the source's pivot rows are taller (or fill the whole tile) and the Sigma pivot shows the same rows at a shorter, fixed height with blank space below, that row-height/stretch difference is this entry. It covers ONLY row height. A pivot that is clipped or truncated, shows fewer rows or columns than the source, cuts off labels or values, sits in a tile that is too small, or uses a cellSpacing preset that does not match the source's density is NOT this entry: those are fixable.
entries.evidence:
Schema: no rowHeight, headerHeight or other data-row-height field exists on pivot-table or TableStyle. The only lever is the 4-step `tableStyle.cellSpacing` preset (extra-large is rejected as an invalid enum), which also sets horizontal cell padding. textStyles fontSize changes text only, and `textWrap: clip` has no effect on pivot headers.

Live probes in org <redacted>, 2026-11-09 (plan C diagnosis R6): the real Complex Pivot (14 rows, 5 regions x 5 measures, Category/Subcategory row headers), rendered at 1000x800 with `display.headerWidths.uniformWidth` 93 and `bodyWidths.uniformWidth` 26. Every probe POSTed 200 and read back clean.
- default / extra-small: 20px data rows; the 14 rows end at y~480 of 800 (~60%). wb 3a89a8d2, wb 92dd1d38.
- small: 23px rows. wb 167e2513.
- medium: 31px rows, ending at y~635; header and value text ellipsize at the 26px width. wb 444acef2, wb 7f1765a8.
- large: 47px rows; padding fills the 26px cells and the pivot overflows 800px after ~12 rows. wb aa243592.
Earlier probe (tableau-to-sigma refs/fidelity-recipes.md "Pivot rows do not stretch with the tile", commit eecfa456, 2026-10-28): growing the tile from 25 to 51 grid rows left the data rows at 48px; the frame grows, the rows do not.

The PNGs were checked directly: r-a-base-1000.png, r-h-small-1000.png, r-i-medium-1000.png, r-d-large-1000.png. Field case: the 2026-11-09 Complex Pivot rerun (wb bd783b70) passed parity, the blind grade and the report, and was blocked at gate 8d only by this delta.

entries.description: A Tableau map can wash out its basemap (Map > Background Maps > Washout, e.g. 25%), which fades the land, water and border layers toward white behind the filled regions. A Sigma region, point or geography map draws its Mapbox base style at full strength and has no washout or basemap-opacity setting, so the basemap behind the fills looks slightly stronger than in the source. The fills, their colors and the base style itself (light, dark, streets, satellite) are unaffected.
entries.evidence: Schema: in the public OpenAPI (assets.sigmacomputing.com, fetched 2026-11-10), region-map mapStyle is oneOf {baseStyle light|dark|streets|satellite, allowZoom, accessToken} | {baseStyle:'custom', styleUrl} | {styleUrl} | null. It has no washout, opacity, fade or basemap-intensity property, and no other region-map property sets one. Live probes (2026-11-10, region-map over a data-model state column): mapStyle {baseStyle:'light', washout:0.25} returned 200 and GET-back dropped the whole mapStyle (workbook 1e921c3b-77e2-43d8-ac35-de4cdcc3ef6e). mapStyle {baseStyle:'light', opacity:0.75} returned 200 and was dropped the same way (8901d218-2f4b-4181-8ab7-7d6f1986350f). Controls: baseStyle 'dark' (9943d17a-02d6-430b-bcc1-b8e7cc566e8f) and 'streets' (49fa0418-48c8-474a-ab2d-4e3a350d075b) round-trip on GET-back, and baseStyle 'light' with allowZoom hidden comes back as {allowZoom:'hidden'} (defd287c-3096-4c66-89b3-5d918284622c), so light is Sigma's default style and is omitted on read. The exported PNG of the washout probe is byte-identical to the plain light-basemap render.

entries.description: A Tableau map (or any sequential color encoding) can use Stepped Color: the measure is binned into N steps (e.g. 8), each region gets one of N flat shades, and the legend shows N swatches. A Sigma scale color is always a continuous gradient between the scheme's colors, so regions with close values get slightly different shades instead of the same step, and the legend is a smooth ramp. The two end colors, the value-to-color direction and which regions are darkest match the source.
entries.evidence: Schema: in the public OpenAPI (assets.sigmacomputing.com, fetched 2026-11-10), the chart/map color oneOf variant {by:'scale', column} allows only scheme ("A continuous gradient needs at least two entries") and domain {min, max, mid}. It has no steps, bins, stepped or interpolation-mode property. Live probes (2026-11-10, region-map over a data-model state column with scheme [#eaf3ea, #2e7d32]): color.steps:8 (workbook 3899c140-2177-4871-824e-ca8715bce45d), color.stepped:true with stepCount:8 (ce1d74b0-8e11-467a-9095-442c53a0cd99) and color.bins:8 with mode:'stepped' (b2f1dd53-8374-4fde-862b-d4a53ea99f6c) all returned 200, and GET-back kept only {by, column, scheme} each time. The exported PNG of the steps:8 probe (viewed) shows a continuous gradient legend, not swatches. Binning the measure into a categorical color column would change the legend and the color assignment, so it is not an equivalent.
